ai.summary: Applies one whole type step — size, line-height, weight, and tracking together — to any element.
whenToUse: A heading, paragraph, or label must match the type scale without hand-assembling four tokens
The consumer's markup chooses the element; the look must come from the system
Display-face headings at weight 800, or muted secondary text
whenNotToUse: Text inside a Button or Card heading slot — those components already apply their own steps
You want to choose the element with a prop — pick the element in markup instead; an `as` prop is how heading levels end up contradicting the outline
Text that is a control — a link is a Link, not styled text
ai.accessibility: Renders no wrapper and no role: the element the consumer chose keeps its semantics, and the component only sets typography. There is no `as` prop by design — an element-choosing prop invites `<h3 as="h2">`-style fixes that contradict the document outline. `muted` sets color only; the muted pair passes the contrast gates in both themes (6.64:1 light).
knownLimitations: There is no `size` prop: `size` is the height scale other components use, and text has no intrinsic height — `variant` names the type step instead
It does not truncate, clamp, or balance lines — layout concerns stay with the consumer
